subject: Regional affinity & archival requirements — follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@hearthtech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@hearthtech.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — data handling & residency questions

Thanks for the call today — this was helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side so we can close the technical qualification before procurement: 

1) Regional affinity: We need to ensure PII stays in-county where possible. For HearthTech EU customers we need strong guarantees that inference and associated logs remain within EU boundaries except for configured failover. Can you outline how Redwood handles region pinning (primary region, allowed failover regions, manual vs automatic failback)? Also, how are replicas/backups handled for model artifacts and logs?

2) Retention windows: We store patient-provided PII for up to 7 years in some markets. We need to understand retention controls (per-customer configurable, retention-at-store vs streaming-only retention) and how Redwood surfaces deletion confirmations/audits.

3) Logging: Access logs and request/response logs — are they redactable at ingest? Are they ever copied out of the tenant region for analytics or support? If we give Redwood limited access for debugging, what controls exist (time-limited session, temp export)?

4) Encryption & keys: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in the EU? If yes, where are keys hosted and who can rotate them?

5) Attachments/questions: We need a simple table mapping our countries of operation to Redwood region options and a recommended failover plan (preferred and allowed). Can you send that as a short matrix?

Next steps: once we have that matrix and short answers above we will share with our security/compliance team (Sarah cc'd) and attempt to put Redwood on our procurement RFP shortlist.

Thanks,
Alex
Principal Product Manager
HearthTech Analytics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@hearthtech.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@hearthtech.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — data handling & residency questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list, really helpful. I'm looping Ben (security & compliance) and Marissa (solutions engineering) to provide short, actionable answers and the country-to-region matrix you requested. High-level answers below; Ben/Marissa will follow up with the matrix and attachments early tomorrow. 

High level: 
- Region pinning: customers can pin inference traffic and storage to a primary region (e.g., eu-west-1). Failover policies are configurable: immediate automatic failover to a pre-approved secondary region, manual failover only, or zone-only failover for short blips. Automatic failover can be restricted to regions within the same geopolitical boundary (EU-only) — that is enforced at the routing layer and recorded in the audit log.

- Backups & replicas: model artifacts (weights) and persistent storage for logs are replicated per the customer's chosen durability profile. By default, backups of model artifacts are stored encrypted in the same region; cross-region backups are opt-in and appear as separate backup objects you must approve.

- Retention & deletion: retention windows are configurable per-customer and per-data-type (inference transcripts, logs, KV cache snapshots). Deletions emit an auditable job ID and time-stamped confirmation; we can provide a CSV of deletion confirmations on request.

- Logging & support access: logs ingested in-region remain in-region unless you grant a temporary support export. Support exports require a ticket and a time-bound approval (single-use URL + expiry). Redaction rules can be applied at ingest (PII regexes) or post-ingest via redaction jobs.

- KMS / CMK: We support customer-managed keys in major cloud regions (AWS KMS & dedicated HSM options). Keys remain under customer control; Redwood performs envelope encryption. Key rotation is available and can be scheduled by the customer; Redwood never sees plaintext key material.

We'll attach a brief residency-affinity matrix and a redlines-friendly SOC2 evidence ask spreadsheet. If that looks good, we can schedule a short follow-up (15–20m) with your security team to confirm constraints and timeline.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@hearthtech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@hearthtech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 07:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — data handling & residency questions

Alex / Sarah — following on Karthik's note, attaching a short residency-affinity matrix (residency-affinity-matrix.pdf) and the SOC2 evidence request template (soc2-evidence-ask.xlsx). Highlights and clarifications from security: 

- EU-only policy: we can restrict both inference compute and request/response logs to EU regions. Automatic failover to non-EU regions requires an explicit policy on the customer's account and is logged with the reason and timestamp.

- Cross-region backups: we keep snapshots (model and config) in-region by default. Cross-region replication is opt-in and can be limited to encrypted archives accessible only via customer CMK.

- Access controls & auditing: all operator actions (including emergency failovers performed by Redwood operators) are recorded in the audit trail. We provide JSON-formatted audit exports on request; these exports themselves can be restricted to S3 buckets in your account.

- Retention proof: when a retention job completes we provide a signed confirmation (job id + SHA256 manifest). For regulatory audits we can provide logs of deletion jobs and key-rotation history.

Attachments in this thread: 
- residency-affinity-matrix.pdf — maps countries to recommended Redwood regions and failover allowances (preferred / allowed / disallowed).
- soc2-evidence-ask.xlsx — spreadsheet listing the evidence types we typically need to accelerate procurement.
- redwood-region-failover-diagram.png — simplified failover diagram.

If HearthTech wants a dedicated private deployment (VPC) in eu-west-1 with backups in eu-central-1 only, we can provide an estimate for Dedicated/Private pricing. Otherwise our hosted configuration with EU-only region pinning usually meets the needs for smaller fleets.

Would you like a 20-minute call Friday to run through the matrix with Sarah?

—Ben
Head of Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@hearthtech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@hearthtech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — data handling & residency questions

Thanks Ben/Karthik — this is excellent and answers most questions. Two quick clarifications before we present to procurement: 

1) For the signed deletion confirmations: can those be pushed automatically to an S3 bucket in our account (we prefer audit artifacts to land in our controls plane)?
2) For KMS: HearthTech uses AWS KMS in eu-west-1 — will Redwood be able to use our customer-managed CMK to encrypt both logs at rest and model snapshot backup objects?

If yes to both, we'll add Redwood to the shortlist and ask procurement to include Dedicated vs Hosted comparative pricing. Sarah — do you have availability Friday 10:00 UTC for a quick call?

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Alex
Principal Product Manager
HearthTech Analytics
